quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and keep both hands on the steering wheel. Slow down and ease back onto the road with a small steering adjustment. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: What happens if you break the rules of a Graduated Driver License?

options.text: It is not a big deal.
You will only get points against your license.
Nothing bad will happen.
You may get a fine and your license may be suspended.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may get a fine and your license may be suspended.
questions.explanation: New drivers with a Graduated Driver License must follow strict driving rules. Breaking these rules may result in a $100 fine and suspension of your license.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. A line through a right turn symbol means no right turn is permitted.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down more.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road, if cars are backing up behind you, you must pull off the road and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane that has the broken line.

questions.question: What problem can a leaking exhaust system cause?

options.text: Using too much oil.
Needing a tune-up sooner than normal.
Making you drowsy while driving.
Starting grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. A leaking exhaust system releases toxic fumes that can make you drowsy while driving and can be very dangerous.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires touching the curb.
Keep the front tires pointing straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill on a street with a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the roadway after a stop, what must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield to the bus.
Speed up to pass the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the bus.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to the roadway after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely return to traffic.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the whole road and both sides of the road continuously.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and both sides of the road continuously.
questions.explanation: To handle dangerous traffic, you must spot and identify problems early. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Continuously scan the entire road and the sides of the road ahead of you.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of the traffic already on the freeway. Always yield to other traffic when merging.

questions.question: If a vehicle is using high beams and coming toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the other vehicle's headlights and lets you see the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Heavy traffic ahead.
Do not enter.
Railroad crossing.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot enter this road or driveway from your current direction. Turn around and find another way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is merging from the right.

questions.question: Your windshield wipers suddenly stop working in rain or snow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Roll down the driver's side window and put your head out so you can see ahead.
Brake and pull off the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down, pull to a safe area off the road, and turn on your emergency flashers. Call for help if needed.

questions.question: What technique helps prevent crashes when driving on ice or snow?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.
Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
Engage four-wheel drive.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snow or ice. Slowing down and leaving more space between you and the car ahead are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.
Be alert for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians cross at this location. Drive carefully and watch for people crossing.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane of the street.
The center of the street.
The left lane of the street.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane of the street.
questions.explanation: Complete your left turn into the left lane. This is the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming up.

questions.question: A vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes starts to lose traction on a slippery road. What should the driver do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer away from danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes automatically, faster than you can. Pumping the brakes or removing pressure will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: A green arrow changes to a solid green light. What does this mean?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may not turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: You can still turn in the arrow's direction, but you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone's blind spot. Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes poor.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, damages your judgment of speed and distance, reduces recovery from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian notices your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter the situation. It is your basic responsibility to watch for pedestrians and yield to all of them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move slowly into each lane as oncoming traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and you can safely make the turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve ahead.
Turn right or left.
Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign means traffic flows only in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Make sure your tires are properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, make sure your tires have good tread and are inflated correctly. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take time to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.
questions.explanation: When driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time before driving to learn where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: You see a crossbuck sign at a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down to listen for a train.
Only cross when a flagger signals you to proceed.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, obey their instructions.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk to warn other cars you are entering.
Stick part of your car into the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you don't see other cars.
Signal only if you see other cars.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you don't see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, turn, or pull away from the curb. Don't skip signaling — it's the law and a safe habit.

questions.question: When you turn right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you can't. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You don't have to stop completely.
Driving is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following, except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. It does not depend on how fit you are or how well you think you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Follow the light unless a police officer is directing traffic — then follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car's headlights are bright, look at the right edge of the road. Don't look directly at the bright lights because it can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Drive the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough space to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the tracks if the warning signal is flashing. Watch for lowered gates or listen for a train before crossing.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.
Help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. Watch carefully for children at school crossings and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car on the left and a bicycle on the right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Drive between them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicycle. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should keep under good driving conditions?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
10 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Use the three-second rule. Pick an object ahead. When the car in front passes it, count three seconds. If your car reaches it after three seconds, you have a safe distance. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, and when following motorcycles or bicycles.

questions.question: A traffic light is not working due to a power outage. What should you do?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers your plans.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. Proceed when it is your turn.

questions.question: A crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone. What must you do?

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, ignore the guard.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from crossing guards, signs, or police in school zones. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point downward. What does this signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following them.

questions.question: To pass a slower car on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Stay on your side of the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming cars.
Use the shoulder.
Cross into the oncoming lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross into the oncoming lane.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must cross into the oncoming lane to pass. Only do this if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: To turn left from a road with multiple lanes in one direction, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start your left turn from the left lane on multilane roads.

questions.question: A driver is entering public traffic from a driveway or private road. What should they do?

options.text: They have the right-of-way.
They should yield to traffic already on the road.
They can force their way into traffic.
They can assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should yield to traffic already on the road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to all drivers on the public road. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light will turn red soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look both ways. Drive through the intersection with caution.
